questions.question: Define a rectangle, a rhombus and a square, and explain how the three are related.
questions.expected_answer: A rectangle is a parallelogram with a right angle; a rhombus is a parallelogram with four equal sides; a square is a rectangle with four equal sides, equivalently a rhombus with a right angle. The square inherits every property of both, so every square is a rectangle and a rhombus, but not conversely.

questions.question: Is every rhombus a kite? Is every kite a rhombus? Give reasons.
questions.expected_answer: Every rhombus is a kite, because its four equal sides give two pairs of equal adjacent sides. Not every kite is a rhombus: a kite with sides 3, 3, 5, 5 has unequal opposite sides and no parallel sides, so it is not a parallelogram.

questions.question: A rectangular gate sags so its angles become 80 and 100 degrees but its sides are unchanged. What is it now and why?
questions.expected_answer: A parallelogram. Both pairs of opposite sides remain parallel and equal, which the definition of a parallelogram requires, but the right angle that made it a rectangle has gone, so it falls to the name directly above rectangle in the family tree.
